annotations.title: Turn a film into a template or a style

description: Make a piece of the working folder out of a film, so it can be used again or shared. As a template: its shots in order with their lengths and choices, its transitions, its music and its finishing; the pictures, the logo, the brand's name and its colours do not leave, and with words: false neither do the texts its author wrote (the library's examples take their place). As a style: its colours, its fonts, its corners and its finishing, never its name or its logo. The piece is then like any other of the folder: start a film from it (create_film { montage }) or dress one in it (edit_film: set_film { look }), check_piece it, and publish_piece it once the user agrees. A template that follows another one too closely is refused when it is shared: the answer says how close this one is.

about.description: One sentence on what it is for, in both languages

as.description: template: the whole film as a film to start from. style: its colours and type alone

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

title.description: The piece's name, in French and in English (not the product's name: others will use it for theirs)

words.description: A template only. false keeps the author's own texts out: the library's examples stand in their place. Default true: they stay as example words
